**Read summary (h4-15041, i18next-http-backend @ 08cb05d):**

One protection, in two copies: `interpolateUrl` applies a per-key URL-segment denylist (`isSafeUrlSegmentBase` + strict-lng / loose-ns helpers) before any loadPath/addPath template reaches `options.request`.

Five candidate traps, all verified in the pinned code:

| id | mechanism | where | why a solver leaves it |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | M8 | `lib/utils.js:35` | shared denylist `[?#%\s]` omits `:`; a value like `http:127.0.0.1:8080` in a template starting with `{{lng}}` becomes an absolute URL |
| T2 | M11 | `lib/utils.js:62-64` | ns helper is a pass-through, so `//evil.example/x` survives; blocking `/` breaks `a/b` and `@org/pkg` |
| T3 | M2 | `i18nextHttpBackend.js:11-28, .min.js:1` | second implementation in generated tsdown output that no test imports |
| T4 | M4 | `lib/index.js:74-84` | `loadUrl` takes a finished URL — looks like the caller's job (uncovered upstream) |
| T5 | M6 | `lib/index.js:56-58, 130-132` | loadPath/addPath functions pre-substitute lng/ns (the repo's own tests do it), so `interpolateUrl` has no placeholders to check |

T1 and T2 are separate groups (a `//` value has no `:`, a `http:` value has no `//`); five independent groups total.

**Usable: yes**, design = T1 + T2 + T3 — three distinct judgements with three distinct dismissals (report-obvious / coupled-value over-hardening, mimo-type / generated artifact, deepseek-type). T4 and T5 are real but excluded because the published fix does not implement them, so fix-derived hidden tests would fail the reference solution.

The load-bearing caveat is in `unverified`: T3 only discriminates if the harness doesn't rebuild (the bundle is `npm run build` output and `npm test` builds first); if it does, the stack collapses to two traps. Also, the fix diff itself wasn't in the worktree, so the exact fix sites (`:` in the base, `//` for ns, bundle regeneration) rest on the screener record plus indirect code/changelog evidence.
